security_audit.summary: The Ruby or shell execution findings are false positives from Markdown code spans, code fences, and TypeScript template literals. The confirmed concerns are the reference links to ../../../.ai files, which traverse outside the skill package into a hidden directory if followed. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious network behavior was found.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle SPEC_FORMAT.md and WORKFLOW.md inside the skill package or link to packaged documentation without ../../../ traversal.
Avoid references to hidden .ai paths. Document required workflow details in visible package files or public documentation.

content.value_statement: Feature work can drift from accepted specs and skip tests. This skill guides agents through acceptance criteria review, TDD, scope checks, and branch or PR handoffs.
actual_capabilities: Reads a subtask specification path before implementation begins.
Asks the user to confirm acceptance criteria before work starts.
Derives test cases from acceptance criteria, including EARS-style criteria.
Guides the Red, Green, Refactor TDD cycle for feature work.
Checks completed work against acceptance criteria before status updates.
Coordinates branch and PR handoff prompts with companion workflows.
limitations: Requires existing EPIC, Story, and Subtask specification files.
Does not create upstream product specifications by itself.
Depends on separate branch and PR skills for those handoffs.
Does not replace security review, code review, or test execution judgment.

use_cases.title: Implement a Defined Subtask
use_cases.description: Follow an approved subtask from acceptance criteria review through tests, implementation, and completion checks.

use_cases.title: Control Scope During Delivery
use_cases.description: Identify requests that are outside current acceptance criteria and ask for a user decision before expanding work.

use_cases.title: Standardize TDD Workflows
use_cases.description: Use a repeatable Red, Green, Refactor process when teams implement features from written specifications.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Subtask
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one defined implementation task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement subtask 001-01-01 using the spec-workflow process. Confirm the acceptance criteria before writing code.

prompt_templates.title: Use EARS Criteria
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with structured acceptance criteria.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use spec-workflow for this story. Convert the EARS acceptance criteria into tests before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Check Scope Before Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request where extra work may appear.
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue this subtask with spec-workflow. Flag any request that is outside the accepted criteria before changing code.

prompt_templates.title: Complete and Prepare Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for completion and review preparation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Finish this implementation with spec-workflow. Verify each acceptance criterion, confirm tests, update status, and prepare the PR handoff.

output_examples.input: Implement the login subtask from the existing specification.
output_examples.output: The assistant presents the acceptance criteria, asks for confirmation, derives tests, and follows the TDD cycle.

output_examples.input: Add CI setup while implementing a configuration subtask.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains that CI setup is outside the accepted criteria and asks whether to defer or create a new subtask.

output_examples.input: Complete the subtask and prepare a review.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks every acceptance criterion, confirms passing tests, updates completion status, and offers a PR handoff.

best_practices: Keep each subtask focused on one feature or behavior.
Confirm acceptance criteria with the user before implementation starts.
Run or review tests at each Red, Green, and Refactor step.
anti_patterns: Starting implementation without a written subtask specification.
Adding related improvements that are not in the acceptance criteria.
Marking work complete before acceptance criteria and tests are checked.

faq.question: Does this skill write specifications?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on implementation after EPIC, Story, and Subtask specifications already exist.

faq.question: Can it work without acceptance criteria?
faq.answer: No. The workflow requires acceptance criteria before implementation starts.

faq.question: Does it require TDD?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill guides work through Red, Green, and Refactor steps.

faq.question: Can it handle EARS notation?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to derive test cases from EARS-style acceptance criteria.

faq.question: Does it create branches and pull requests directly?
faq.answer: It prompts handoffs to companion branch and PR workflows. Those workflows must be available separately.

faq.question: Is this a security review skill?
faq.answer: No. It improves implementation discipline, but separate security and code reviews are still needed.
